summary: A seven-turn multi-domain back-office session: retrieve airline booking A58410 (T1), handle an impossible passenger-update request (T2), book a Seattle car rental (T3), recover from a server error to run a three-part shopping/document task (T4-T5), execute a nine-part batch of lookups, searches, a spreadsheet edit, a cart add, and a policy summary (T6), then recap (T7). The cognitive high point is T2, where the agent reasons that two things are true at once — there is no update_passengers tool and the requested names already match the record "character for character" — so the task is both unnecessary and impossible, a clean Evaluate + Deciding move. T5 and T6 are enormous confirmation dumps that even cite specific tool calls ("I queried the rental record directly via get_car_rental", "Verified by reading back the saved file"). As a CONTROL baseline, two defects persist: T4 leaks a raw 500 Internal Server Error to the user with no reflection, and across the data-heavy turns the component_timeline classifies every call as generic other with zero retrieval — so the named-tool verification claims in T5-T6 are not corroborated by the component trace.
